title: The 152-ФЗ consent gate — one canonical record, three screens, and two bundles whose submit always fails
why:
Three deployed bundles each carry their own consent screen, and they have drifted apart. `app.html` runs the canonical `AMayaConsent` and writes to `/client-channel/consent`; `app-tenant.html` and `maya-os-site/index.html` still run the older `AConsentGate` against the PHP relay; and `app.html` keeps a retired stub of that old gate — `function AConsentGate() { return null; }` (app.html:25143) — still mounted beside its replacement (app.html:39613) under a header comment that still describes the relay flow. The record itself is not duplicated: both routes end at one writer, `submitConsent` (client-channel-runtime.service.ts:187), reached directly (client-channel.controller.ts:121) and, via the bot's `/api/consent/submit` and the legacy bridge to the same service, indirectly (:259). The duplication is in the screens and the front doors, not in the store.

The two legacy screens cannot write at all. They submit `{accept_pdn: true, accept_marketing: …}` with no command identity, and a stable idempotency key is required twice over — at the relay (package5-client-consent-proxy.php:16, which answers `400 invalid_client_command`) and again by the canonical writer itself. Relaxing the relay check would not fix it; the field has to be sent, as `app.html` already sends it. Until then those clients are held by a gate they cannot pass, and see «Не удалось сохранить. Попробуйте ещё раз.» every time.

Each legacy copy also decides for itself who is exempt (`__meCurMode === 'staff'`, app-tenant.html:12208, maya-os-site:22047), how support forces the screen open (`?consent=1`), and what happens when the status call fails — a 401 there silently switches the gate off (app-tenant.html:12219-12232). And because both legacy bundles fetch their policy text from the salon's own relay, a white-label tenant's client is shown «ИП Мосин Станислав Евгеньевич, ИНН 263409096156» as the operator of their own data (webhook_server.py:4440, served at :4786). A consent record is a legal artifact; three screens, three exemption rules and someone else's operator name is the defect, not the UI.
disappear:
The per-bundle copies: the two legacy `AConsentGate` screens, and in `app.html` the retired stub together with its mount and its stale header comment. The PHP relay hop for `consent_submit` (api-proxy.php → package5-client-consent-proxy.php) — but only after a working ingress is in `app-tenant.html` and `maya-os-site/index.html`; removing it first leaves those two bundles with no consent write at all. The retired Telegram accept callbacks, which today collapse `pdn_accept` / `mkt_accept` / `mkt_decline` into a single redirect to the app (bot.py:1751-1756). The passive booking-consent footnote in `app.html` legacy mode stops existing as a thing of its own — it has no checkbox, no receipt and no server call, and must never be counted as consent.

What does not disappear is the full-screen consent surface itself; only its three separate implementations do. And this entry does not settle which front door onto the one writer survives — the PWA's direct `/client-channel/consent` or the bot's `/api/consent/submit`, which the group's own proposed successor names. Both reach the same record; picking one is a decision still to be made, not a fact being reported.
remain:
The consent record and its two independent decisions — personal data required, marketing optional. The canonical writer already stores them as two separate facts and already accepts a "no"; it is all three screens that can only ever transmit "yes" (`{privacy: true, …}`, app.html:25243; `accept_pdn: true` in both legacy copies), with nothing but a client-side tick in front of it. The successor must take the recorded decision from what was actually submitted, on the server.

The policy text remains a capability, with one correction to how it is carried across: what the legacy screens show is an excerpt, rendered only in the "sign the consent" state and never in the marketing-only one, and it names the salon as operator. Port the rendering, not the text — the successor needs the operator identity of the tenant whose client is reading it. (The full policy is shown before acceptance only in Telegram.)

The two states driven by server `status` — the full screen when personal-data consent is missing, the shorter «Рассылки» re-ask when only the marketing choice is outstanding. The behaviour that staff are not gated and that support can force the screen open, with the exemption decided on the server as `AMayaConsent` already does rather than by a client-side mode flag, and with the force-open unable to write a fresh record for a client who already has one. The booking-confirm slot keeps both of its branches: the legacy 152-ФЗ notice and the SaaS calendar-destination string that shares the slot.

And the gate keeps blocking — as a verified full-screen surface. Under the widget contract the consent kind may show the decision and hand off to that surface; it may not carry the accept control and collects nothing (§2.6.18 CONSENT.1, CONSENT.4, fullscreen required), and until the consent read capability is registered it cannot carry even the handoff (`GAP-CONSENT-READ`). Chat may bring the client to the gate; the signature stays on the surface. One property no copy has today must also be built in: when the status call fails, the gate fails closed.
risk:
HIGH — and live now, not something the merge would introduce. Of the 126 rows in this dossier, every consent row sits in this one group (checked across all 26). Today: clients on the tenant and MayaOS bundles cannot record consent by any route, because every submit is rejected before it becomes a record; a Telegram client who cannot reach the app has no in-channel route either, since the consent buttons only redirect while the `group=-1` gate stops every non-exempt update (bot.py:4973); a refusal cannot be expressed anywhere, because acceptance is a constant in all three screens; and the gate switches itself off when its own status call fails — narrowly and recoverably in the legacy copies (401 only, retried every 800 ms), broadly and without recovery in the canonical one, where any 5xx on `/client-channel/status` hides the gate until the session token next rotates (app.html:25220, 25229). A tenant's client is additionally shown the wrong data operator.

The merge is the repair; the hazard is the status quo persisting — together with four ways to make it worse: copying the salon's policy text into a tenant's screen, keeping acceptance as a client-side constant, collapsing the two decisions into one "I agree", and inheriting the canonical component's silent self-disable as if it were the safe behaviour.
user_impact: Clients notice this, not staff and not the owner (all three gates are roleMode:client and bypass staff). Today a client in the salon app (app.html) is the only one on a live write path: AMayaConsent → `/client-channel/consent`. A client on the white-label tenant bundle (app-tenant.html) or on the stale maya-os-site/index.html bundle hits a full-screen blocking gate — `position:fixed; inset:0; zIndex:100000`, no dismiss control — whose Submit always fails: both build the body via `__meAuthReq({accept_pdn:true, accept_marketing:!!mkt})` (app-tenant.html:12261, maya-os-site:22100) without `idempotency_key` (`grep -c` = 0 in both), and the live relay hard-requires `is_string(idempotency_key)` (package5-client-consent-proxy.php:16-17, reached for `consent_submit` per the sanitized Beget api-proxy fixture:2128-2132), so every submit returns 400 `invalid_client_command` and the gate shows «Не удалось сохранить. Попробуйте ещё раз.» forever. Two scoping conditions the raw claim omits: the gate only appears for an already-logged-in client whose `consent_status` is not `pass`, and a 401 on that status call sets `done = true` and silently removes the gate entirely. A Telegram-only client gets no consent path (bot.py:1752-1757 collapses pdn_accept/mkt_accept/mkt_decline into a redirect to APP_URL). Two corrections to what is said to be lost. First, the tenant and MayaOS gates are NOT "the only places a client is shown the actual policy text" — they render `_PRIVACY_SHORT` (webhook_server.py:4440-4446), an excerpt whose own comment says «полная версия — у бота PRIVACY_TEXT», behind a collapsed disclosure that is only rendered in the `need_pdn` branch, never in the marketing-only «Рассылки» state; the full policy is shown before accept in Telegram (S-653 `pdn_policy` → PRIVACY_TEXT, bot.py:1747-1749), which the sweep itself calls the only full-policy pre-accept surface in the estate and classes KEEP AS CAPABILITY, outside this group. Second, the loss that field names is smaller than the defect it would carry: both bundles fetch that excerpt from the salon's own relay (`CONSENT_PROXY = 'https://malesthetic.pro/app/api-proxy.php'`, app-tenant.html:12165, maya-os-site:22004), so it names «ИП Мосин Станислав Евгеньевич, ИНН 263409096156» as the operator to a white-label tenant's client — porting that rendering as-is is the wrong instruction; the successor needs a per-tenant operator identity, not a copy. What the merge actually gives those clients is one consent step that writes at all; whether it is "inside the chat run" for a Telegram-only client is not established by this merge — Gate G20 («consents written on channel identity alone 0») and the A18 reason recorded at bot.py:1751 are exactly why that callback writes nothing today.
security_impact: Mixed, not a net improvement, and one sub-claim points the wrong way. Real improvement: two of the three live bundles record no 152-ФЗ consent at all today because every submit is rejected at the relay before reaching Maya, so a merge onto a live write creates records where none currently exist. But which write is not settled: this group's own PROPOSED SUCCESSOR names `/api/consent/submit` (aiohttp, webhook_server.py:10015, bot SQLite), while app.html uses `/client-channel/consent` (NestJS, client-channel.controller.ts:121, Postgres). These are different systems in different stores and are not interchangeable; asserting the consolidation direction as decided overstates what has been approved. Direction error to correct: retiring the legacy `401 → _unauth → done = true` branch (app-tenant.html:12219-12232) is presented as closing a fail-open, but the component being consolidated onto fails open wider and without recovery. AMayaConsent sets `checkedSession = signature` BEFORE the status fetch and does not reset it in the `.catch`, which does `setShow(false)`; `meWidgetAf`'s `finalize` throws on any `!r.ok`, so one 500/503/network blip on `/client-channel/status` suppresses the gate for the rest of that token's life, because the 800ms interval short-circuits on `checkedSession === signature`. The legacy gate fails open only on an explicit 401 and on 5xx/network resets `checkedRef.current = false` and retries every 800ms — it recovers. The merge therefore replaces a narrow recoverable fail-open with a broad permanent one unless the successor is built otherwise. Two checks that genuinely must be re-established: (1) `accept_pdn` / `privacy` is a transport constant on every copy — hardcoded `true` in both legacy gates (app-tenant.html:12261, maya-os-site:22100) and `{privacy:true, marketing:!!mkt}` in the canonical one — and the legacy early-return is itself guarded by `status === 'need_pdn'`, so the marketing-only «Рассылки» state re-sends `accept_pdn:true` with no tick and no guard at all; "a refusal cannot transport as an acceptance" is a property the successor must be built to have and inherits from nothing. (2) The gate must fail closed on a status-fetch error, which no existing copy does. Correction to the staff-exemption claim: `window.__meCurMode === 'staff'` is a property of the two legacy copies only (app-tenant.html:12208, maya-os-site:22047) and has zero relevance in the successor's base — AMayaConsent gates on `meAppAccessCurrentMode() !== 'client'`, `__meAppMode` is resolved only from the server's `app_access` contract («Persist only a server-returned mode», app.html:5680-5707), and eligibility is decided by the server's `/client-channel/status`. The role determination is already server-side there; what remains client-side is only whether to render. Finally, nothing here may promise a Telegram-channel consent write: Gate G20 requires «consents written on channel identity alone 0», and bot.py:1751 records that a Telegram callback identifies a channel, not a Client.
